title: Control Plane Standup — Roundtable Fragments (2026-09-05)
content:
Date: 2026-09-05
Attendees: Priya (owner), Liam, Sofia, Ethan, Maya (SRE drop-in), Aaron (rotations) — +1 slack presence from Product

Purpose: quick roundtable focusing on emergent token churn, routing quota drift observed in canary, and auth migration timing. This doc captures fragments and action items for follow-up; not a polished minutes doc.

Agenda:
- Quick metrics snapshot
- Token TTL / KV cache growth discussion
- Routing quota enforcement flakiness in us-west-2 canary
- Auth v2 rollout blockers & rollback playbook check
- Short-term mitigations and owners

Snapshot (last 24h metrics):
- Control plane API 95th pctl latency: 78ms (up from 62ms baseline)
- Token churn rate: +12% week-over-week (spike coincident with nightly job at 03:10 UTC)
- Quota enforcement error rate (canary): 0.48% failures, most are 429->500 translation edge cases
- Auth token validation latency: median 2.1ms, tail 22ms (increased since TTL change)

Notes / Discussion:
1) Token TTL increase experiment (PR merged last week) likely responsible for KV cache size growth. Liam ran heap profiles — there is ~9–12% uptick in per-shard mem usage on allocator nodes when the new TTL hits 1.5M active keys. We need a rollback gating metric: if mem delta > 8% across 50% shards within 6h, rollback automatically.

2) Routing quota drift: canary region (us-west-2) showing quota enforcement messages getting queued in the router -> occasionally routing->quota service RPCs time out causing retries and double-debits in some reporting. Sofia noted an uninstrumented code path in the router that re-enqueues on timeout; need quick fix to ensure idempotent debit.

3) Auth v2 rollout: current blockers are (a) missing KMS key permission mapping for enterprise customers, (b) lack of opt-in toggle in Dedicated control plane console. Product asks for a soft opt-in before GA. We sketched the toggle UX; Aaron to coordinate.

4) Incident mitigation discussed: short-term guardrails:
   - Revert TTL PR if mem delta threshold breached (owner: Liam, target: +4 hours monitoring, ETA: 2026-09-06 12:00 UTC)
   - Add a middleware timeout/backoff for router->quota RPCs to avoid re-enqueueing (owner: Sofia, branch: hotfix/router-quota-timeout, ETA: 2026-09-08)
   - Add a sanity check in quota service to reject duplicate debit attempts when request idempotency key present (owner: Ethan, spike underway)

5) Rollback playbook review: we rehearsed the rollback checklist for auth v2 and TTL changes. Action: update playbook with automatic metric gating and who calls the rollback (SRE on-call + Platform owner). Priya to update doc by 2026-09-07.

Decisions made:
- Hold full auth-v2 universal rollout until KMS permission mapping is resolved; proceed with opt-in for selected enterprise tenants.
- Promote router-hotfix to canary tomorrow after unit tests; do not promote to prod until duplicate debit mitigation is in place.

Action items (owner — due):
- Liam Chen — add mem-delta alert and automated rollback wiring for TTL PR (due 2026-09-06 12:00 UTC)
- Sofia Martinez — implement router backoff/hotfix branch + test matrix for 429/timeout cases (due 2026-09-08)
followups: Priya to update rollback playbook (confluence) by 2026-09-07
Ethan to finish idempotency spike and link PR
Maya (SRE) to run a focused load test on allocator nodes simulating TTL 1.2M keys
